comment: This class is the {@link RopeByteString} equivalent for {@link ByteArrayInputStream}.

variables.name: pieceIterator
variables.comment: Iterates through the pieces of the rope

variables.name: currentPieceSize
variables.comment: The size of the current piece

variables.name: currentPieceIndex
variables.comment: The index of the next byte to read in the current piece

variables.name: currentPieceOffsetInRope
variables.comment: The offset of the start of the current piece in the rope byte string

variables.name: mark
variables.comment: Offset in the buffer at which user called mark();

methods.name: public int read(byte[] b, int offset, int length)
methods.comment:
* Reads up to {@code len} bytes of data into array {@code b}. * *

Note that {@link InputStream#read(byte[], int, int)} and {@link * ByteArrayInputStream#read(byte[], int, int)} behave inconsistently when reading 0 bytes at * EOF; the interface defines the return value to be 0 and the latter returns -1. We use the * latter behavior so that all ByteString streams are consistent. * * @return -1 if at EOF, otherwise the actual number of bytes read.

methods.name: private int readSkipInternal(byte[] b, int offset, int length)
methods.comment:
* Internal implementation of read and skip. If b != null, then read the next {@code length} * bytes into the buffer {@code b} at offset {@code offset}. If b == null, then skip the next * {@code length} bytes. * *

This method assumes that all error checking has already happened. * *

Returns the actual number of bytes read or skipped.

methods.name: private void initialize()
methods.comment: Common initialization code used by both the constructor and reset()

methods.name: private void advanceIfCurrentPieceFullyRead()
methods.comment:
* Skips to the next piece if we have read all the data in the current piece. Sets currentPiece
     * to null if we have reached the end of the input.

methods.name: private int availableInternal()
methods.comment: Computes the number of bytes still available to read.
